text: I think the experience changed my whole approach to stress. Before, I treated every stressful event as an emergency. My body would go into full alarm mode: racing heart, shallow breathing, tunnel vision. I'd either attack the problem frantically or freeze completely. During the experience, there was a long stretch where I was overwhelmed by fear and I couldn't do anything about it, I couldn't fix it or escape it. My guide encouraged me to just notice the fear, where it was in my body, what it felt like, without trying to change it. After a while it shifted on its own, and I was left with this incredible stillness. I've used that lesson countless times since. When I get bad news or something goes wrong at work, I first notice what's happening in my body. I breathe, I feel my feet on the ground, I let the alarm settle a bit. Then I decide what to do. It sounds simple, but it's completely changed how I deal with stress. I make better decisions and I don't exhaust myself.

Ich bin seitdem gelassener und kann mit Unsicherheit besser leben. Das hat mir vor allem bei der Jobsuche nach dem Studium geholfen, die sich sehr lange hingezogen hat. Ich habe darauf vertraut, dass es irgendwann klappt.

I've become better at handling stress because I'm more connected to my own values. I used to make decisions based on what other people expected of me, and I was constantly stressed because I was living a life that didn't fit. During the experience I got very clear about what I care about, and since then I've made some big changes: I left a corporate job and now work for a small nonprofit. I earn less, but I'm much less stressed, and when difficult things happen at work I feel they're worth it.

The experience helped me deal with something very specific: the stress of being the child of an alcoholic father who is now dying of liver disease. For years I avoided him because every interaction left me shaking and angry. During the experience I had a long encounter with my father as a little boy, scared and lonely in his own father's house. I understood that his drinking came from a pain he never dealt with. I didn't forgive him exactly, but the anger softened into something more like sadness. When he got sick, I was able to visit him in hospital and actually be there, without needing him to apologise or change. We had some honest conversations in his last months, and I said what I needed to say. It was the most stressful period of my life, but I got through it without falling apart and without regrets. My wife and my therapist were a big support, and I let them be.
Ich bin ruhiger geworden, wenn es Ärger gibt, und kann besser abwarten, statt sofort zu reagieren. Das hat sich vor allem bei Streit mit meinen Eltern positiv ausgewirkt.
I'm more okay with discomfort now, so stressful things don't knock me over like they used to.

My experience was with ayahuasca in a ceremonial context, and it was very difficult. The first night I was confronted with all the ways I had hurt people in my life, my ex-girlfriends, my brother, my mother. It was like a film playing in front of me, and I couldn't look away. I felt crushing guilt and shame. On the second night, I was shown the same scenes, but this time from a place of compassion, and I understood why I had acted the way I did: I was hurt, scared, and I didn't know better. That shift from shame to compassion has changed how I deal with stressful situations, especially conflict. When I mess up now, I can acknowledge it and apologise without collapsing into shame. That makes it much easier to repair things. I've also become much more careful about how I treat people when I'm stressed, because I don't want to add to that film. My relationships are healthier, and I feel more at peace with myself even when things go wrong.

Ich habe das Gefühl, dass ich mich durch die Erfahrung selbst besser kennengelernt habe. Ich weiß jetzt, welche Situationen mich besonders stressen, nämlich wenn ich mich ungerecht behandelt fühle, und kann mich darauf einstellen.

Since the experience I've been a lot better at handling the stress of my chronic illness. I have type 1 diabetes, and managing it is a constant source of low-level stress, plus the occasional crisis. I used to feel resentful and angry about it all the time. During the experience I felt very connected to my body and actually grateful to it for keeping me alive despite everything. That gratitude has stayed with me, and it makes the daily management feel less like a burden. When I have a bad hypo or my numbers are all over the place, I'm calmer and less hard on myself.
I don't feel the same pressure to be perfect. I make mistakes and I move on.

Die Erfahrung hat mir sehr geholfen, mit dem Stress umzugehen, den mein Beruf als Krankenpflegerin auf einer onkologischen Station mit sich bringt. Ich habe jeden Tag mit Leid und Tod zu tun, und lange Zeit habe ich das einfach weggesteckt. Irgendwann hatte ich Schlafprobleme, war gereizt und habe mich innerlich leer gefühlt. In der Erfahrung habe ich all die Trauer gespürt, die ich über die Jahre angesammelt hatte. Ich habe um viele Patientinnen und Patienten geweint, die ich begleitet habe. Danach war ich erschöpft, aber auch erleichtert. Seitdem versuche ich, meine Gefühle nach schwierigen Diensten zuzulassen, statt sie zu verdrängen. Ich habe eine kleine Routine entwickelt: Ich zünde eine Kerze an, denke kurz an die Menschen, die gestorben sind, und lasse sie gehen. Außerdem spreche ich mehr mit Kolleginnen über belastende Erlebnisse. Ich fühle mich heute viel stabiler und kann meinen Beruf wieder mit Freude ausüben.
I'm better at recognising when I'm overwhelmed and stepping away. Before, I'd just keep pushing until I broke down.

I think the biggest change is that I've learned to be more patient with myself during difficult times. I used to expect myself to bounce back immediately from any setback, and when I didn't, I'd get angry with myself, which made everything worse. Now I give myself time. When my business partner left last year, I allowed myself a few weeks to feel disappointed and lost before making any decisions. It turned out to be the right approach.
Ich bin nicht mehr so schnell gekränkt und kann Kritik besser annehmen. Dadurch entstehen weniger Konflikte, und ich bin insgesamt weniger gestresst.

I came to the experience after a long period of burnout. I had been on sick leave for three months and I felt completely empty. I'd tried everything: therapy, medication, a stress management course. Nothing seemed to reach the core of the problem. During the experience, I finally understood what that core was. I'd been living my whole life as if I had to justify my existence through work. If I wasn't productive, I wasn't worth anything. I saw where this came from, my father, who only praised me when I got good grades, and I felt so much grief for the little boy who worked so hard for his father's love. Since then, I've been able to handle stress at work very differently. I don't take on every task anymore. I leave on time. When something goes wrong, I don't see it as a judgement on my worth. I've been back at work for over a year now and I haven't relapsed. My colleagues have noticed that I'm calmer and more relaxed, and I even enjoy my job again.
More able to take a step back and think before I react

Ich habe in der Erfahrung gelernt, dass ich nicht alles kontrollieren kann, und das hat mir sehr geholfen, mit Stress umzugehen. Früher habe ich versucht, jede mögliche Katastrophe im Voraus zu verhindern. Heute lasse ich die Dinge eher auf mich zukommen und reagiere dann.

I've become better at handling stress because I'm not so isolated anymore. Before the experience I was very much a loner. I didn't really have close friends and I dealt with everything on my own. The experience made me realise how lonely I was and how much I wanted connection. Since then, I've made an effort to build friendships. I joined a running club and a book club, and I've gotten close to a few people. When stressful things happen now, I have people to talk to, and that makes a huge difference.

I'm in recovery from an eating disorder, and stress used to trigger restriction every time. If I felt out of control, I'd control my food. During the experience I felt my body from the inside, really felt it, maybe for the first time since I was a child. I felt how hungry and tired it was, and how hard it had been working to keep me alive while I was starving it. I cried for a long time and I promised my body that I would take care of it. That promise has stayed with me. When stress hits now, I notice the urge to restrict, and I remember that promise. I don't always manage, but most of the time I eat anyway. I've also found other ways to deal with the feeling of being out of control: I journal, I go for gentle walks, I talk to my dietitian or my best friend. My treatment team says I've made more progress in the last year than in the five years before.
Ich gehe mit Belastungen gelassener um, weil ich weiß, dass ich sie bewältigen kann. Ich habe in der Erfahrung sehr viel Angst gehabt und habe sie überstanden. Das gibt mir Zuversicht.
I find it easier to forgive people who cause me stress, and that means I don't carry it around as long.
I would say I'm about the same in how I deal with stress, but I'm more aware of what's happening when I'm stressed.

Seit der Erfahrung gehe ich mit belastenden Ereignissen grundlegend anders um. Ich bin vorher ein sehr ängstlicher Mensch gewesen, der bei jeder Kleinigkeit das Schlimmste befürchtet hat. Wenn mein Mann sich verspätet hat, dachte ich sofort an einen Unfall. Wenn ein Brief vom Amt kam, hatte ich Herzrasen. In der Erfahrung habe ich eine tiefe Ruhe und Geborgenheit erlebt, wie ich sie noch nie gekannt hatte. Ich hatte das Gefühl, dass ich nicht allein bin und dass das Leben mich trägt. Diese Erfahrung ist wie ein Anker für mich geworden. Wenn heute die Angst kommt, erinnere ich mich an dieses Gefühl, und es hilft mir, ruhiger zu werden. Ich habe außerdem gelernt, meine Ängste mit meinem Mann zu teilen, statt sie für mich zu behalten. Er war sehr erleichtert, weil er oft nicht wusste, was mit mir los war. Insgesamt ist mein Leben viel entspannter geworden.
I'm more grounded and I take things one step at a time instead of panicking about everything at once.

I've learned that I tend to catastrophise, and I've developed some strategies to deal with it. When I notice my mind running to the worst-case scenario, I ask myself what the most likely outcome is. Usually it's much less dramatic. I also remind myself that even if the worst does happen, I'll find a way to cope. That was something I really felt during the experience, a deep sense that I can handle whatever comes. It's made stressful events much less frightening.
Ich nehme mir in stressigen Zeiten bewusster Zeit für mich, z.B. für einen Spaziergang oder ein heißes Bad. Früher hätte ich das als Zeitverschwendung empfunden.

It's been about three years since my experience, and I think one of the most lasting effects has been on how I handle stress in my relationship. My partner and I have been together for twelve years, and we'd gotten into some bad patterns. When either of us was stressed, we'd snap at each other, and small arguments would turn into big fights. We took mushrooms together at a cabin, with a friend as a sitter. At one point, we were lying next to each other and I suddenly saw him as if for the first time, this beautiful, vulnerable person who I love so much. He said he had the same experience with me. We cried and talked for hours. Since then, when we're stressed, we try to remember that moment. We've gotten much better at telling each other what we need, and at giving each other space when we need it. We still argue, but it's different, there's more tenderness in it. When my mother got sick last year, we handled it together as a team, and I don't think I could have done it without him.
I'm less worried about things I can't control. I focus on the present.

Ich habe gemerkt, dass ich bei Stress oft unbewusst die Luft anhalte und die Schultern hochziehe. Seitdem achte ich darauf und atme bewusst aus, wenn ich das bemerke. Das hilft mir erstaunlich gut, ruhiger zu bleiben.

I'm much better at dealing with uncertainty, which used to be my biggest stressor. I'm a freelancer, and I never know where my next contract will come from. I used to lie awake at night worrying about money. During the experience, I felt a deep sense of trust in life, and that has stayed with me. I still plan and save, but I don't panic when things are quiet. Somehow, work always comes in the end, and I've learned to believe that.
About the same as before, I'd say. Maybe I'm a bit more relaxed but I'm not sure it's because of the experience.

Die Erfahrung hat mir geholfen, eine sehr schwierige Phase in meinem Leben zu bewältigen. Ich war damals arbeitslos, frisch getrennt und hatte große Geldsorgen. Ich fühlte mich als Versager und hatte manchmal Gedanken, dass es besser wäre, nicht mehr da zu sein. Ein Freund hat mich zu einer begleiteten Zeremonie mitgenommen. In der Erfahrung habe ich gespürt, dass mein Leben wertvoll ist, unabhängig davon, ob ich einen Job habe oder in einer Beziehung bin. Ich habe auch gespürt, wie sehr mich meine Freunde und meine Familie lieben. Das hat mir neuen Mut gegeben. In den Monaten danach habe ich mir Hilfe gesucht, eine Therapie angefangen und mich bei verschiedenen Stellen beworben. Heute habe ich wieder einen Job und eine neue Partnerin. Wenn ich heute in eine schwierige Situation komme, erinnere ich mich an das Gefühl, dass mein Leben wertvoll ist, und dass ich nicht allein bin. Das hilft mir, nicht in Verzweiflung zu verfallen.
Less irritable when stressed, I don't take it out on others as much.
My experience was mostly positive, but I don't think it changed how I handle stress. I still get stressed, I still deal with it the same way, by going to the gym and talking to friends.
Ich bin gelassener und kann mit stressigen Situationen besser umgehen. Ich lasse mich nicht mehr so leicht aus der Ruhe bringen und behalte eher den Überblick.

I struggled with severe social anxiety for most of my life, and social situations were my biggest source of stress. Job interviews, parties, phone calls, even ordering at a restaurant would make me sweat and shake. During the experience I had an intense feeling of love and connection to other people, all people, and I suddenly saw how much I'd been hiding from them out of fear. I saw that people are mostly kind and that they are as scared as I am. That changed something deep in me. Afterwards I started exposing myself to social situations bit by bit, with the help of a therapist, and it's been so much easier than before. I recently went to a friend's birthday party where I knew almost no one, and I actually enjoyed it. I still get nervous, but it doesn't control my life anymore. Stressful social situations have become manageable, and other kinds of stress feel smaller too, because I'm not constantly exhausted from anxiety.
I'm more patient and I don't let small problems ruin my day

Ich habe durch die Erfahrung ein besseres Gespür dafür bekommen, was mir guttut und was nicht. Ich habe danach einige Veränderungen in meinem Leben vorgenommen: Ich habe meine Arbeitszeit reduziert, mich von einer belastenden Freundschaft getrennt und angefangen, regelmäßig Sport zu machen. Dadurch habe ich weniger Stress und kann mit dem verbleibenden Stress besser umgehen. Ich merke auch schneller, wenn mir etwas zu viel wird, und kann rechtzeitig gegensteuern.
It made me less reactive and more thoughtful when things go wrong.

Leider habe ich nach der Erfahrung über Monate mit Ängsten gekämpft, und belastende Situationen haben diese Ängste immer wieder verstärkt. Ich bin vorsichtiger geworden und meide manche Situationen, z.B. große Menschenmengen.
